solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fantastic new skill flipping nose holding tip

indicators.note: flipping turns the word for skill over, so it reads backwards

parts.note: art is skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: holding means the word for nose wraps round the word for tip

parts.note: a nose, in the sense of a smell or a wine's bouquet, is a scent
an end is a tip, as in the end of a stick

explanation.surface: Praise for a nimble new trick in which someone turns over while balancing on the end of their nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nose' reads as the body part but is a smell; 'flipping' and 'holding' look like parts of the acrobatic trick yet are the signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Transcendent is used loosely to mean beyond the ordinary, so fantastic or superb in praise.

clue.text: Current odds for Thorpe in crawl

indicators.note: odds means take the letters in odd positions, first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: The betting odds on the swimmer Ian Thorpe in a freestyle race.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Thorpe was an Australian Olympic swimmer; crawl is the freestyle stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means of current interest, relating to present events.

clue.text: Stood with sailor on deck, both half-cut

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: both half-cut means each of the two words loses half its letters, keeping the front half

explanation.surface: A drunken sailor and his mate standing on deck, both tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it halves 'on' to O and 'deck' to DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Abode is an old past tense of abide, to tolerate, so stood as in stood for it.

clue.text: Look almost embarrassed admitting retreat's blocked

indicators.note: admitting means letting the retreat in between the shortened look's letters
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to see is to look
a nook is a secluded retreat; the 's is read as is, a link
red, as in red-faced, means embarrassed

explanation.surface: Someone looks sheepish on being told their escape route is cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' shortens the word for look, and 'admitting' lets a retreat inside it; 'blocked' is a snooker term for a player with no clear shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker a player blocked from hitting the target ball is snookered, so blocked or thwarted.

clue.text: Eat out, and so on, on husband

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and so on

explanation.surface: Dining out, and so forth, at the husband's expense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' suggests a restaurant but means corrode.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by corroding, eating away at, its surface.

clue.text: Very French, turning tail in action, fled

indicators.note: in puts the reversed word inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action

indicators.note: turning tail means the word goes back to front

parts.note: très is French for very

explanation.surface: A French soldier ran away in battle, turning tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' looks like flight, but it turns TRES into SERT, which goes 'in' DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon a post and run off, so deserted means fled.

clue.text: Stocking, any long stocking?

indicators.note: stocking means holding in stock, so these words contain the answer

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether any long hosiery is in stock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking' is used twice: first as hosiery, then as the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A nylon is a stocking made of that synthetic fibre, usually said in the plural.

clue.text: From heart of Japan, the only temple

indicators.note: from heart of says the answer lies inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Japan's one and only temple, at the centre of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is a temple to all the gods, most famously the one in Rome.

clue.text: Beware edges of rocks? They should

parts.note: cave, Latin for beware, is old school slang for watch out

indicators.note: edges of means take the first and last letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A warning to beware the edges of rocks, and who should heed it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: potholers should indeed beware edges of rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Potholers exploring underground should watch out for sharp rock edges, so they are the ones who should.

clue.text: Nose about into old relative following endless search

indicators.note: following tells us the remaining pieces come after the shortened search
endless means the last letter of the word for search is cut off

parts.note: to probe is to search or investigate

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for about goes inside the word for relative

parts.note: sis, short for sister, is a relative
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A nosy busybody pokes around an elderly relation after an unsuccessful search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nose about' looks like a phrase for prying, but 'Nose' alone is the definition and 'about' is C, signalled into the relative by 'into'; 'endless' trims the search.
explanation.definitionFit: A proboscis is an elongated nose or snout, used humorously of a large human nose too.

clue.text: Capital city of USA about endures

indicators.note: about means the city's letters go round the word for endures

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, an American city
has, in the sense of has to put up with, means endures

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which American capital city lasts the longest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital city' looks like one phrase, but only 'Capital' is the definition; 'city of USA' is LA, wrapped 'about' HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, so it is a capital city in its own right.

clue.text: Showing some front, or rear?

definitions.meaning: front here means boldness or nerve, so showing some front is being impudent
the question mark invites reading the word as of the backside, which has cheeks

explanation.surface: A teasing question whether someone is displaying their front or their back.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheeks are the buttocks, so a cheeky rear is a joke on the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent behaviour is called cheek, and showing front means showing nerve, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Make beer clear, they say, with dark head

indicators.note: they say signals the words are heard as they are spoken, not as they are spelt

parts.note: to make beer is to brew; net (or nett) means clear, as in clear profit

explanation.surface: A home brewer fining a beer until it is clear, with a dark head of foam like stout.
explanation.walkthrough: BREW NET, said aloud, matches the word meaning a dark-haired woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A brunette is a woman with dark brown hair, so a dark head of hair describes one.

clue.text: Lags inside facing endlessly rigorous sentences initially

definitions.text: Lags inside facing endlessly rigorous sentences initially

indicators.note: initially says take the opening letter of each of the preceding six words

parts.words: Lags inside facing endlessly rigorous sentences

explanation.surface: Convicts in prison face long, harsh sentences from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: those serving life terms do face endless, rigorous sentences.
explanation.definitionFit: Lags are convicts in British slang, and those serving life sentences are the longest-staying prisoners.

clue.text: Soft soap less frothy on youngster's head

parts.note: flatter, of a drink, means with fewer bubbles

indicators.note: head means the first letter of the word that precedes it

explanation.surface: A soap that lathers less, applied to a child's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft soap' looks like a washing product but means flattering talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft soap is persuasive praise, excessive compliments used to win someone over.

clue.text: Turbulent struggles with son after wife's left

indicators.note: after places the son's letter at the end
left means gone, so the abbreviation for wife is taken out

parts.note: wrestles means struggles, as with a problem
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A family in turmoil: the son fights after his mother walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a direction but signals removal of W from WRESTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means unsettled and agitated, as is turbulent water or a turbulent mood.

clue.text: Artist's first to underwrite rubbish as well

indicators.note: underwrite says these letters are written under the others in this down light

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish
too means as well
the 's stands for is

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An artist is the first to guarantee rubbish too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underwrite' means insure, but in a down clue it puts IS and the first letter of 'to' beneath TAT and TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: One who inks designs on skin is an artist of a kind, so a tattoo artist.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly's reportedly creepier in front

parts.note: an ant is a creepy-crawly; the 's is a link

indicators.note: reportedly signals that a word is heard spoken rather than seen written

parts.note: eerier means creepier

explanation.surface: Talk of an insect that is creepier at its front end.
explanation.walkthrough: ANT plus a word for creepier, spoken, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anterior is the anatomical term for situated towards the front.

clue.text: In earnest, and in general, upright

indicators.note: In tells us the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone sincere and generally honest is upright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In earnest' reads as a phrase meaning seriously, but 'In' is the signal and the letters run across 'earnest, and in general'.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing means erect, on one's feet, as does upright.

clue.text: Retiring having also consumed drink

indicators.note: consumed means taken in, so the word for retiring swallows the word for also

parts.note: retiring means shy
and means also

explanation.surface: A shy person who has also had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' suggests going to bed but means shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a drink.

clue.text: Verse talks about gutted Antipodean soldier, mostly

indicators.note: about here means turned round, reversing the remaining pair
gutted means the inside of the word talks is removed, leaving its outside letters
mostly means drop the last letter

parts.note: an Anzac is a soldier from Australia or New Zealand

explanation.surface: A poem tells of a disembowelled Australian soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' leaves TS of 'talks', which 'about' turns to ST; 'mostly' cuts ANZAC to ANZA.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Dull article on individual about empty day

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: about means the word for individual goes round the emptied day

parts.note: one is an individual

indicators.note: empty means remove the middle, leaving the outside letters

explanation.surface: A boring newspaper article about one person with nothing to do all day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a piece of journalism but is the grammatical article; 'empty' keeps only the outside of 'day' and 'about' wraps the individual round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means bland and inoffensive, so dull.

clue.text: Solicitor advanced, still returning to collect rent

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: to collect means the reversed word gathers in the word for rent
returning means the word for still is read backwards

parts.note: yet means still, as in yet more
rent, the past of rend, means torn

explanation.surface: A lawyer moves forward, still coming back to gather the rent owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money paid to a landlord but is the past of rend; 'returning' turns the word for still round and 'to collect' takes it in.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US an attorney is a lawyer, the counterpart of a British solicitor.

clue.text: Material from Queen certainly being played

parts.note: R, for Regina, is Queen
ay means yes, certainly
on means happening or being played, as a match is on

explanation.surface: A musical tribute to the band Queen, playing some material.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen the band misleads; it is R for Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: Rayon is a synthetic fabric, so a material.

clue.text: Coverage for South American Open?

parts.note: reads like broadcast coverage of a tennis or golf tournament, but means a garment covering a South American, open at the sides

explanation.surface: Television coverage of a sporting tournament held in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: A poncho is a blanket-like cloak with a hole for the head, worn in South America and open at the sides.

clue.text: Heartless beauty caught rising star

indicators.note: rising, in a down light, means the letters read upwards
heartless means one of the middle letters is removed

parts.note: a belle is a beauty
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A cruel beauty was caught as her star rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' cuts BELLE to BELE; with C, 'rising' reverses the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Celeb is short for celebrity, a famous person or star.

clue.text: Attack over loud argument

indicators.note: over means turned over, reversing the word

parts.note: a fit is an attack of illness or temper
F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud

explanation.surface: A noisy row turns into a physical assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attack' reads as the subject of the sentence but is a fit of temper, turned 'over'; 'loud' is the musical forte.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a small quarrel, a minor argument.

clue.text: Bowler seen in local competition

definitions.meaning: a bowler is a hard round felt hat, which Americans call by this name
a match between two neighbouring teams of the same area

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler appearing in a neighbourhood contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' suggests cricket, but it is the hat; a local derby is a match between rival teams from one town.
explanation.definitionFit: The American name for the bowler hat and the British name for a contest between local rivals.

clue.text: First XI's carrying idiot partner

indicators.note: carrying means the eleven's letters hold the word for idiot between them

parts.note: XI is eleven, which written in figures, 11, looks like two letter I's
a nit, short for nitwit, is an idiot
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A cricket team's first eleven having to carry a useless teammate.
explanation.walkthrough: XI, a cricket team of eleven, is written 11 and read as II.
explanation.definitionFit: Initially means at first, at the start, so first as an adverb matches it.

clue.text: A French master's story about sex is useless

parts.note: un is French for a
a pro, a professional, is a master of a craft

indicators.note: about means the word for story goes round the word for sex

parts.note: a fable is a story
it is a coy word for sex, or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A French teacher's tale about sex is judged worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'master' looks like a schoolmaster here but is a PRO.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprofitable means yielding no gain or benefit, so useless or fruitless.
